issue.title: replace tool normalizes literal backslash-n into a newline in Rust source
issue.body:
Observed while implementing UQM S4 evidence validation with LLxprt Code on macOS.

The `replace` tool changed a replacement containing a Rust byte literal for newline into a physical newline inside the literal. A follow-up call supplying two different strings, one containing the physical newline and one containing the literal backslash followed by `n`, returned `No changes to apply. The new content is identical to the current content`.

Expected: exact text replacement should distinguish a physical newline from a literal backslash plus `n`. JSON transport escaping should not cause an additional unescape pass in the replacement text.

Observed source after replacement:
```rust
assert_eq!(bytes.pop(), Some(b'
'));
```
Intended source:
```rust
assert_eq!(bytes.pop(), Some(b'\n'));
```

This caused a Rust compiler error: `byte constant must be escaped: \n` at `rust/xtask/src/ci/evidence.rs:14203`. The subsequent unified-diff tool preserved the intended literal. No LLxprt source changes were made.

Local evidence in the UQM checkout: `tmp/issue34-astra-s4-v2/session-20260907-s4-5163/red-trace-newline.log`. The corrected behavioral RED run is separately retained in `red-trace-newline-corrected.log`; the first log records the tool-induced source error, not the intended regression failure.

steps: Create sample.rs with exactly this one-line Rust source and a final newline: fn main() { let x = 0; }. Read it with read_file.
expected: Exact replacement preserves literal source-code escape sequences after JSON decoding.
defect: replace writes physical newline/CR control characters where new_string contained literal backslash escape sequences, corrupting source code.
Root cause: The observed behavior is consistent with an additional escape-normalization step after JSON decoding, which makes literal backslash-n indistinguishable from an actual newline. The reports do not identify a confirmed implementation line; do not label an arbitrary edit helper as the root cause.
